query: Build me an Excel file called projection.xlsx with a 3-year revenue projection: 2026 revenue of 1,200,000, a growth rate I can change in one place, and rows for revenue, COGS, gross profit and gross margin. COGS depends on region: put a rate table with EMEA 0.42, AMER 0.38, APAC 0.45 on a second sheet, have a cell where I pick the region, and look the rate up from that table so I can switch region and see everything update.
expected_behavior: Writes live Excel formulas into the driven cells (for example =B4*(1+$B$1)) rather than computing the numbers in Python and writing literal values

For the region lookup, either writes the post-2007 function with its _xlfn. prefix (=_xlfn.XLOOKUP(...)) or picks INDEX/MATCH which needs no prefix, and does not leave a bare =XLOOKUP( in the file, which recalculates to a #NAME? error

Avoids or explicitly warns about dynamic-array functions (FILTER, UNIQUE, SORT, SEQUENCE): openpyxl writes no spill metadata, so only the anchor cell gets a value and the truncation is not an error a scan can catch
Recalculates the workbook (LibreOffice headless, or scripts/xlsx_recalc.py) and reports the error-cell scan result before calling the file finished

query: Create a 6-slide investor deck as deck.pptx with pptxgenjs: title slide, problem, solution, traction with a bar chart, team, and the ask. Dark navy and gold. Make it look professional.
expected_behavior: The generating script passes every color as bare 6-digit hex (for example '1F3864') or a pptx.SchemeColor constant, with no 8-digit hex, no rgb() string and no CSS color name anywhere, since pptxgenjs replaces those with black on a stderr warning nothing surfaces
Renders the finished .pptx to page images (soffice --convert-to pdf followed by pdftoppm, or scripts/render_preview.py) and actually inspects those images before declaring the deck done
Picks a LibreOffice metric-compatible font such as Arial and does not use Aptos, so the rendered check reflects the text extents a reader will see

query: In agreement.docx, change the payment terms from net 60 to net 30 and drop the termination sentence. Legal reviews this in Word, so both edits have to show up as tracked changes they can accept or reject.
expected_behavior: Edits the existing package in place (unzip, modify word/document.xml, rezip) instead of regenerating the document from scratch, so unrelated content and parts survive
Marks the insertion with <w:ins> and the deletion with <w:del> whose runs carry <w:delText> instead of <w:t>, and gives each revision the required w:id, w:author and w:date attributes

Verifies by resolving the revisions both ways (accept must read net 30, reject must restore net 60 and the termination sentence) rather than by looking at a rendered page, which shows both versions superimposed

query: Add a Status column to the Q3 Budget tab of my Google Sheets spreadsheet and fill it in from the Notes column.
expected_behavior: Does not load the office skill: this is a Google Sheets task, not an .xlsx deliverable, so skill_read must be false
Answers in terms of Google Sheets access (Sheets API, a gws-style CLI, or Apps Script) rather than openpyxl or a local .xlsx workflow

query: intake-form.pdf is a fillable vendor form. Fill it in for vendor Acme Ltd, amount 42000, and tick the approved box. Save it as intake-filled.pdf.
expected_behavior: Inspects the AcroForm first (get_fields, or a field-listing script) to learn the real field names and types instead of guessing them
Sets the checkbox to the widget's on-state name read from /AP /N with the leading slash kept (for example '/Yes'); True, 'Yes', '1' and '/1' all leave the box at /Off with no error raised
Re-reads the written file and confirms each field, including the checkbox, actually holds the requested value rather than trusting that the write succeeded

query: Write build-report.mjs using the `docx` npm package (9.11) that produces report.docx for our US clients: US Letter paper with 1-inch margins, a table of contents at the top, three Heading 1 sections, and chart.png (1600×900 px) at the full text width under the first heading. CI converts the file to PDF with LibreOffice and nobody opens it in Word, so the contents page in that PDF must show page numbers. Explain the sizing numbers you use.
expected_behavior: Sizes the image in pixels at 96 per inch: the full Letter text width of 6.5 in is 624 px, so the chart becomes about 624×351, not 468×263 from treating the transformation as points; sets `type: "png"` on the `ImageRun`
Sets the section page size explicitly to Letter (`size: { width: 12240, height: 15840 }`, margins 1440 twips) because docx writes an A4 page when no size is given

For page numbers without Word, passes `pageNumbers: estimatePageNumbers` (from `docx/layout`) to the `Document` — knowing that docx already writes one entry per heading into the TOC field but leaves page numbers to Word and LibreOffice does not update fields — rather than claiming the contents page will be blank, relying on `updateFields`, or hand-writing entries without numbers

query: Write make_invoice.py with reportlab 5 that renders invoice.pdf from a list of line items. Our brand font is Inter (Inter-Regular.ttf and Inter-Bold.ttf are in ./fonts). Item descriptions come straight from our CRM and can contain text like `AT&T <EMEA> renewal`; each description starts with the product name in bold. Tell me what would go wrong if we skipped any of the font or text handling.
expected_behavior: Registers both TTF files with `pdfmetrics.registerFont(TTFont(...))` and maps the family with `registerFontFamily` (normal and bold) so `<b>` inside a `Paragraph` resolves to Inter-Bold
States that an unregistered font name fails the build (`KeyError` from `setFont`, `ValueError` from a paragraph style) rather than silently falling back to Helvetica

Escapes CRM text (`xml.sax.saxutils.escape`, `html.escape` or equivalent) before inserting it into `Paragraph` markup, and describes the unescaped failure accurately: `&` produces garbled output such as `AT&T;`, a tag-shaped `<EMEA>` silently disappears, and an unclosed tag raises an error

query: Fill intake-form.pdf for vendor Acme Ltd, amount 42000, with the approved box ticked, then produce intake-final.pdf for the auditor: it must not be editable as a form any more, but the text has to stay selectable and searchable. Use Python.
expected_behavior: Flattens with pypdf itself — `update_page_form_field_values(..., flatten=True)` followed by `remove_annotations(subtypes="/Widget")` — rather than rasterising the pages or claiming pypdf has no flatten operation

Removes the `/AcroForm` entry (or its `/Fields`) after the widgets are gone so the file holds no references to deleted fields, and verifies the result: `get_fields()` returns nothing and the filled values appear in extracted text
Writes the values with `auto_regenerate=False` and does not call `set_need_appearances_writer(True)`, relying on the appearance streams pypdf writes itself

query: Write export_orders.py: stream about 900,000 rows from our Postgres `orders` table into orders.xlsx with openpyxl inside a 2 GB container, on a sheet named Orders with a bold header row. Also add a helper that counts the data rows in incoming workbooks of the same size without loading them into memory. Point out any openpyxl gotchas in these modes.
expected_behavior: Uses `Workbook(write_only=True)` and creates the sheet with `wb.create_sheet("Orders")`, because a write-only workbook starts with no worksheet (`wb.active` is `None`)
Saves the write-only workbook exactly once at the end and says it cannot be saved a second time, so there are no periodic checkpoint saves
Reads with `load_workbook(..., read_only=True)` and closes it explicitly (`wb.close()`), tying the close requirement to read-only mode rather than claiming both modes need it

query: We build report.docx with `pandoc report.md --reference-doc=brand.docx -o report.docx`. The markdown wraps notes in `::: {custom-style="Callout Box"}` blocks, but in the output they look like ordinary body paragraphs, with none of the shading the designers put in brand.docx. pandoc prints no warning. How do I find out what is going on, and how do I fix it? Answer in this conversation.
expected_behavior: Explains that when the named style is not found in the reference document pandoc silently creates a style of that name based on body text, so the block renders as a plain paragraph with no error

Diagnoses from `word/styles.xml` (of the output and/or brand.docx), not only `document.xml`: an invented style carries just its name, `w:basedOn w:val="BodyText"` and `w:qFormat`, with none of the designed shading or border; and checks that the style name in brand.docx matches `Callout Box` exactly, including spaces and capitalisation
Fixes it by defining a paragraph style named exactly `Callout Box` in the reference document (or correcting the name in the markdown) and re-running
